This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 8 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/tx/austin/KAUS.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the National Weather Service and AccuWeather indicate Austin highs near 98–99°F on August 8 under mostly sunny conditions, aligning with the 57.5% market-implied probability for that bin and the 23% for 96–97°F. This reflects typical late-summer climatology, where the monthly average high reaches 98°F amid a regional heat dome that has sustained triple-digit readings earlier in the week. Recent model runs show slight cooling from 100–101°F peaks on prior days, with limited moisture supporting only spotty afternoon activity unlikely to suppress the maximum. Official observations from Camp Mabry will resolve the market, and any last-minute shifts in steering patterns or cloud cover could adjust final readings within the narrow 96–101°F range dominating trader consensus.
